topic.name: Interpreting the Meaning of the Derivative in Context

question.text:
The function $V(t)$ models the number of visitors, in thousands, to a new website, $t$ hours after the website's launch. What is the best interpretation of the statement below?

$\qquad$ The slope of the tangent line to the graph of $V(t)$ at $t=10$ is equal to $1.5.$
question.choice1: $10$ hours after launching, the number of visitors increased at a rate of $1\,500$ visitors per hour
question.choice2: $10$ hours after launching, the number of visitors increased at a constant rate of $150$ visitors per hour
question.choice3: $10$ hours after launching, the number of visitors decreased by a total of $1\,500$ visitors
question.choice4: $10$ hours after launching, the number of visitors increased by a total of $1\,500$ visitors
question.choice5: $10$ hours after launching, the number of visitors decreased at a rate of $1\,500$ visitors per hour
question.explanation:
The slope of the line tangent to the graph of $V(t)$ at $t=10$ gives the derivative of $V(t)$ at $t=10.$ So, we have that

\[ V'(10)=1.5. \]

We can interpret the above statement as

$\qquad$ $10$ hours after launching, the number of visitors increased at a rate of $1\,500$ visitors per hour.

example.title: Interpreting the Derivative of a Function in a Given Context

question.text:
Joseph is measuring the weight gain of his pet puppy by recording the following two numbers for different values of $t,$ where $t$ is the time, in days, since he started his observations:

  • $W(t)$ - The puppy's weight, in kilograms

  • $r(t)$ - the rate at which the puppy's weight is increasing.

What is the relationship between $W(t)$ and $r(t)?$
question.explanation:
The function $W(t)$ gives the weight of the puppy after $t$ days. Then, \[ W'(t) = \dfrac{\textrm{d}W(t)}{\textrm{d}t} = \dfrac{\textrm{Change in }W}{\textrm{Change in }t}. \]

Thus, $W'(t)$ gives the rate at which the weight of the puppy increases at time $t$, which is the same as $r(t).$ Therefore, the relationship between $W(t)$ and $r(t)$ is $W'(t) = r(t).$

example.title: Relating a Derivative to a Rate of Change

question.text: In a factory, the cost of producing an item depends on the number of items produced per day. The function $U(x)$ models the cost, in dollars, to produce an item if the factory is producing $x$ items per day. What is the best interpretation of $U'(500)=0.01?$
question.choice1: When the factory produces $500$ items per day, the cost per item increases at a rate of $0.01$ dollars per item
question.choice2: When the factory produces $500$ items per day, the cost per item is $0.01$ dollars
question.choice3: For the first $500$ items produced, the cost per item constantly increased at a rate of $0.01$ dollars per item
question.choice4: For every $500$ items produced, the cost per item increases by $0.01$ dollars
question.choice5: When the factory produces $500$ items per day, the cost per item is $5$ dollars
question.explanation:
The function $U'(x)$ represents the rate at which the cost changes when the factory produces $x$ items per day.

Therefore, $U'(500)=0.01$ means:

$\qquad$ When the factory produces $500$ items per day, the cost per item increases at a rate of $0.01$ dollars per item
